Regrowth after partial hepatectomy

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A healthy adult undergoes removal of part of the liver. During recovery, growth signals induce surviving hepatocytes to enter the cell cycle, increasing the number of viable cells in the remnant. Which process chiefly restores cell number?

  1. Squamous metaplasia
  2. Coagulative necrosis
  3. Disuse atrophy
  4. Dystrophic calcification
  5. Compensatory hyperplasia
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Compensatory hyperplasia

Hepatocytes can re-enter the cell cycle and proliferate in response to growth signals after tissue loss.

Understanding the options

Compensatory hyperplasia
Hepatocytes can re-enter the cell cycle and proliferate in response to growth signals after tissue loss.
Squamous metaplasia
Squamous metaplasia would change epithelial phenotype rather than restore hepatocyte number.
Coagulative necrosis
Necrosis decreases viable tissue mass.
Disuse atrophy
Disuse atrophy reduces cell size and organ mass.
Dystrophic calcification
Calcification deposits calcium rather than replacing functional cells.
